title: Alexander of Aphrodisias, In Aristotelis Analyticorum priorum librum I commentarium, ed. M. Wallies (CAG II.1; Berlin: Reimer, 1883)
edition: Wallies 1883, the First1KGreek TEI (from the Internet Archive scan), with Wallies's pages and line numbers

license.payload: Alexander (fl. c. 200 CE) and Wallies 1883 are public domain. CC BY-SA 4.0 (the TEI packaging, as stated in the file's teiHeader); the archive asserts no further licence.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only.

normalization:
The TEI as fetched under original/. text/ is the reduced by code (prepare_texts38.py): teiHeader, note, app and bibl dropped; one line per

, or ; each numbered

marked [ ]; the edition's page breaks stand as [p. N] and its numbered lines as |L. No text was corrected by hand. The file's line numbers also carry the manuscript's folio marks (|40r) and some numbers out of sequence; a locus is cited by its [p. N] and the Wallies line numbers that bracket it.
scope: Book I whole: the commentary that names the ἑταῖροι of Aristotle, Theophrastus and Eudemus, against him on the modal mixtures.
why_seated: The first surviving witness who reads the Prior Analytics with its school beside it: the ἑταῖροι dissent at 124.5–10 (cited as 124.8).
verified_loci: 124.5–10, the companions dissent on the mixture of necessary and assertoric — 'οἱ δέ γε ἑταῖροι αὐτοῦ οἱ περὶ Εὔδημόν τε καὶ Θεόφραστον οὐχ οὕτως λέγουσι' (text/in-apr-i.txt)
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-11-14 01:25 EST: "lets continue to assemble and we'll deposit and seat the whole thing as a massive batch"; the standing rule for originals-library seatings, 2026-10-18: "original language where available always".

research.study: Critique of Pure Inference (working draft v1.1) and The Production of Readers (#1767), §11.6 "the witnesses between"
research.for: the reception history of inference from the Peripatos to the machine: the commentators who name Aristotle's ἑταῖροι, the Latin handbooks, the early-modern refusals of the syllogism, the nineteenth-century rebuilds, and the traditions that reasoned about inference without the Organon
